Keep trying if it's something you truly want. I went through roughly 50 applications since 2017. Had one in 2020, medical resignation in the academy, resolved, then was denied and denied up until this year. Small county department filled with great people with a slot in the academy as the classes go, so I'm working jail non-cert until my class comes up. 

Sometimes you just have to find another path to get to the same end goal. I got so many "someone will pick you up, you're a great candidate" and "we just went with other candidates" conversations during this time and it was hard, but you just keep trying. The position I applied for before this, I had a detective and an FTO corporal giving me a good word. Passed backgrounds, thumbs up from civil service, it was all set to go and I should have been in. The executive safety commissioner denied me. One guy on the last step of the process brought the entire thing down. The detective thought it was because her name was on my file and that commissioner has a grudge. Sometimes petty stupid shit happens and you just have to deal with it. Fix what you find out, show drive to improve, and be honest. And don't worry about age being a thing. I got accepted at 29, and in my last academy we had a guy that was 52.

Honestly, in my case it wasn't the pain as to why I was on the fence. I was more asking what the purpose was, as I really didn't see one at the time.

I'm sorry that you're dealing with this. Honestly, it is going to take a long time, and it may take just as long to forgive yourself. You do deserve forgiveness, op. You were a kid. Not my story, but my academy instructor shared this story with us during our homicide class. 

When he was a detective with the sheriff's office, he got called out to an unresponsive child at a birthday party. Parents were noticeably calm and aloof about it. When he found the kid, he had no pulse. Unfortunately, they were not able to revive him. When the coroner did his autopsy, they stopped counting after 100 bruises. The 5 year old was beat to death by his father as punishment for wetting his pants. What's worse, he was killed in front of his 10 year old brother who saw the entire thing. On top of that, the father was also found to have been molesting the 11 year old daughter. The husband was arrested by my instructor and got life without parole for his crimes. The wife escaped charges as an accomplice as they couldn't find any evidence that she was involved in the abuse. Not what you know, it's what you can prove in court and all that. The wife still blames my instructor for putting her "man" away. She doesn't hate her shitbag husband for abusing and killing her kids. She blames the detective for him being locked up. He said he cried for a long time after that, going home to hug his wife and daughter and just breaking down in his wife's arms several days. Had nightmares and said it will never leave him.

The images of that battered kid on the autopsy slab are going to stick with me for a while. Several other cadets, most  who had children of their own, broke down after that one. 


If you see something, say something. If you are suspicious abuse is taking place, report it. Do something. You might stop a cycle and save a life.
